message.content:
You are reviewing a freshly written JavaScript port of part of PyYAML for
fidelity. Read /workspace/spec/PORTING.md first, then read representer.mjs and serializer.mjs in
/output/lib/ closely.

The author's own notes: Wrote /output/lib/serializer.mjs (SerializerMixin) and /output/lib/representer.mjs (RepresenterMixin), faithful ports of PyYAML 6.0 serializer.py and representer.py.\n\nserializer.mjs: ANCHOR_TEMPLATE 'id%03d' on the prototype with a hand-rolled %03d formatter; open/close/serialize/anchorNode/generateAnchor/serializeNode; anchors and serializedNodes are identity-keyed Maps, reset at the end of serialize(). serializeNode computes detectedTag/defaultTag via resolve(ScalarNode, value, [true,false]) / ([false,true]) for scalars and passes the bare boolean `true` as `implicit` for collections, exactly as PyYAML does.\n\nrepresenter.mjs: BaseRepresenter (represent, representData, representKey, representScalar, representSequence, representMapping, ignoreAliases, representedObjects/objectKeeper/aliasKey) + SafeRepresenter + the full-Dumper Representer overrides. Registries are module-level Maps keyed by pyTypeName, exposed on the prototype as yamlRepresenters/yamlMultiRepresenters and reached via `this.`; a pyMro() helper supplies bool->int and datetime->date. `id(data)` is modelled as the data object itself, so recursion through representedObjects works as in PyYAML. representMapping sorts a *copy* (Python's sorted() builds a new list, so a TypeError leaves insertion order intact) using pySortInPlace + pyLessThan on [key, value] arrays, catching PyTypeError.\n\nVerified against /workspace/dataset/test4_executable with a stub emitter/resolver harness: sorted dicts, alphabetised !!set, float fixups (1.0 / 1.0e+17 / 1.0e-05 / -0.0 / .nan / .inf / -.inf), !!binary 76-col wrap with trailing newline and style '|', !!python/tuple for omap, alias emission, unsortable-key fallback, and self-referential lists all match.\n\nTwo corrections to the brief, both confirmed empirically: (1) the serializer error string is 'serializer is not opened', not 'open() first' — I inflated the PyInstaller zlib streams in the reference binary and grepped the marshalled constants; (2) anchor ids are handed out in SECOND-encounter order, not first — '{a: &x [1], b: &y [2], c: *y, d: *x}' yields a: &id002 / b: &id001 from the binary, and the port reproduces that.\n\nBoth files import only from ./errors.mjs, ./nodes.mjs, ./events.mjs, ./pytypes.mjs. No RegExp, no JSON, no require, no backslash-u escapes; both parse and import cleanly under node.
Their stated uncertainties: Constructor options convention. PORTING.md only says 'constructor reads options'. Both mixins call a local dumperOptions(args) that scans args[1..] for the first non-null object argument, i.e. they expect `new Dumper(stream, { defaultFlowStyle: false, sortKeys: true, encoding, explicitStart, explicitEnd, version, tags, defaultStyle })` with camelCase keys. If dumper.mjs uses a different shape the options are silently ignored — but the defaults I chose (defaultFlowStyle false, sortKeys true, everything else null) are exactly what yaml.dump(..., default_flow_style=False) needs, so even a mismatch produces correct output for this program. Worth confirming with the integrator.; Empty-mapping flow style. The brief asked representMapping to 'mark a mapping as flow when it is empty'. PyYAML does NOT do this in the representer — it is emitter.py's check_empty_mapping() inside expect_node. I left it out. If '{}' does not come out as '{}', the fix belongs in emitter.mjs, not here.; Collection `implicit` argument to resolve(). PyYAML passes the bare boolean `True` (not a 2-element array) for SequenceNode/MappingNode, and I ported that literally. resolver.mjs must therefore only index implicit[0] when kind is ScalarNode; passing `true` will not crash in JS (true[0] is undefined) but would differ from Python if the resolver indexes it unconditionally.; representObject / representUndefined. PyYAML's full Representer registers a copyreg-driven represent_object as the `object` multi-representer. Nothing safe_load produces can reach it, so mine raises RepresenterError('cannot represent an object'). PyYAML's represent_undefined passes a second arg (`RepresenterError("cannot represent an object", data)`), which errors.mjs's single-argument RepresenterError cannot carry; the message text is right but a Python traceback would show the tuple form. Unreachable in this program.; Omitted registrations with no JS analogue: complex, types.FunctionType/BuiltinFunctionType/ModuleType (represent_name/represent_module), and collections.OrderedDict (represent_ordered_dict). I confirmed from the binary's marshalled constants that these exist in the real representer.py, but safe_load cannot construct any of them.; pySortInPlace is a binary-insertion sort. That matches CPython's list.sort() for n < 64 but not the merge phase for larger mappings. Since a dict's keys are pairwise unequal, the comparison sequence only affects WHICH comparison raises first, so a >64-key mapping with mixed key types could in principle keep insertion order under one algorithm and raise at a different point under the other. Both still end up keeping insertion order, so I believe this is unobservable, but I did not test a large mixed-key mapping.

Your job is to find and FIX real porting defects in those files. Look for:
- logic that silently diverges from PyYAML (off-by-one on indent/column, a
  missing branch of a fetch_*/expect_*/construct_* method, a dropped error case,
  wrong operator precedence when a Python 'and/or' became '&&/||')
- hand-written matchers that do not accept exactly the language the original
  regex accepted (test the boundaries)
- Python truthiness or int-division semantics that do not survive translation
- constraint violations: any RegExp use, any JSON reference, any non-relative
  import, any literal backslash-u escape in the file, a missing .mjs suffix
- Python's 'is None' vs falsy: a JS 'if (x)' where PyYAML wrote 'if x is not None'
  and 0 / '' / false are legitimate values

Verify behaviour against the reference binary
(/workspace/dataset/test4_executable --a '...') wherever a question is settleable
that way. Do NOT run python.

Edit the files in place to fix what you find. Do not touch other modules, and do
not rewrite working code for style. If a whole-pipeline test is impossible
because sibling modules are still landing, reason locally and note it.

Report the defects you fixed and anything still suspicious.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Porting contract: PyYAML → JavaScript (ESM)
2	
3	We are reimplementing, from behaviour, the exact subset of PyYAML that this
4	Python program exercises:
5	
6	```python
7	result = yaml.dump(yaml.safe_load(args.a), default_flow_style=False)
8	print(result)
9	```
10	
11	Reference binary (ground truth, run it freely):
12	`/workspace/dataset/test4_executable --a '<yaml>'`
13	
14	It is PyYAML **6.0**-era behaviour (`\/` escape supported; timestamps keep
15	`tzinfo`; fractional seconds are truncated to 6 digits, never rounded).
16	`yaml.dump` uses the **full `Dumper`**, not `SafeDumper` — so `tuple` is
17	represented as `!!python/tuple`.
18	
19	## HARD CONSTRAINTS — a violation invalidates the whole deliverable
20	
21	1. **ESM only.** `import` / `export`. No `require`, no `module.exports`.
22	2. **`.mjs` suffix** on every file, and every relative import must spell the
23	   suffix: `import { x } from './chars.mjs'`.
24	3. **Zero external dependencies.** Only relative imports of our own files.
25	   No npm packages. No `node:` built-ins either, except that the entry point may
26	   use `node:process`-style globals (`process.argv`, `process.stdout`).
27	4. **No `RegExp`, ever.** No regex literals (`/.../`), no `new RegExp`, no
28	   `.match()` / `.matchAll()` / `.search()`, and no regex argument to
29	   `.replace()` / `.split()`. String arguments to `.replace()`, `.replaceAll()`,
30	   `.split()`, `.indexOf()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()` are fine. Every
31	   pattern PyYAML expresses as a regex must become an explicit character-by-
32	   character matcher function.
33	5. **No `JSON`.** Do not reference `JSON.parse`, `JSON.stringify`, or any other
34	   member of it, anywhere — not even in a comment or a debug line.
35	6. **Never write a `\uXXXX` escape into a source file.** The authoring pipeline
36	   decodes those into raw characters. Import the character you need from
37	   `./chars.mjs`, or build it with `String.fromCharCode(0xNNNN)`. `\n`, `\t`,
38	   `\r`, `\0`, `\xNN` escapes are safe to write.
39	7. **No Python.** Do not shell out to python, and do not embed Python source.
40	
41	## Style
42	
43	Terse, idiomatic modern JS. camelCase methods. Keep the port structurally
44	line-for-line with PyYAML so it can be audited against the original: same method
45	decomposition, same control flow, same error strings. Where a PyYAML regex
46	becomes a hand-rolled matcher, put the original pattern in a comment above it.
47	Comment density: sparse — only where the port diverges from PyYAML or where the
48	character-level logic is not self-evident.
49	
50	## Composition: mixins, not multiple inheritance
51	
52	PyYAML builds `Loader` and `Dumper` by multiple inheritance over mixin classes.
53	In JS each module exports a **mixin factory**:
54	
55	```js
56	export const ScannerMixin = (Base) => class extends Base { /* ... */ };
57	```
58	
59	`loader.mjs` / `dumper.mjs` (written by the integrator, not you) compose them:
60	
61	```js
62	class Root {}
63	const Loader = ResolverMixin(ConstructorMixin(ComposerMixin(
64	  ParserMixin(ScannerMixin(ReaderMixin(Root))))));
65	```
66	
67	Consequences you must respect:
68	
69	- All mixins share one `this`. Initialise your own state in the constructor
70	  after `super(...args)`. The constructor receives whatever `new Loader(text)`
71	  is called with — pass args through with `super(...args)`.
72	- You may freely call methods defined by *other* mixins on `this`
73	  (e.g. the scanner calls `this.getMark()`, the composer calls `this.resolve()`).
74	- Do not redefine a method another mixin owns.
75	
76	## Foundation modules (already written — import, do not modify)
77	
78	### `./chars.mjs`
79	Named characters and character sets, all built with `String.fromCharCode`:
80	`NUL BELL BACKSPACE TAB LF VTAB FF CR ESC SPACE NEL NBSP LS PS BOM`,
81	`LINE_BREAKS` (`\r\n` + NEL + LS + PS), `LINE_BREAKS_Z` (NUL + those),
82	`BLANK_Z` (NUL, space, tab, breaks), `SPACES` (` \t`), `BLANK` (spaces+breaks),
83	`DIGITS`, `HEX_DIGITS`, `LETTERS_DIGITS`, `ALPHA` (letters+digits+`-_`),
84	`EMIT_ESCAPES` (Map char → escape letter), `SCAN_ESCAPES` (Map letter → char),
85	`SCAN_ESCAPE_CODES` (Map of `x`→2, `u`→4, `U`→8).
86	
87	### `./errors.mjs`
88	- `Mark(name, index, line, column, buffer, pointer)` — `buffer` is an **array of
89	  single-code-point strings**; `pointer`/`index`/`column` are code-point counts.
90	  `toString()` reproduces PyYAML's `  in "<unicode string>", line N, column M:`
91	  plus snippet and caret.
92	- `YAMLError`, `MarkedYAMLError`, and the marked subclasses
93	  `ScannerError, ParserError, ComposerError, ConstructorError`, each constructed
94	  as `new ScannerError(context, contextMark, problem, problemMark, note?)`.
95	- `ReaderError(name, position, character, encoding, reason)`.
96	- `EmitterError(msg)`, `SerializerError(msg)`, `RepresenterError(msg)`.
97	- `PyValueError(msg)`, `PyTypeError(msg)` — stand-ins for the builtin Python
98	  exceptions PyYAML lets propagate. Every error carries `.qualifiedName`
99	  (e.g. `'yaml.scanner.ScannerError'`, `'ValueError'`) for the traceback printer.
100	
101	### `./pytypes.mjs`
102	Python value semantics. **Python `int` is `BigInt`; Python `float` is `number`.**
103	That distinction is load-bearing: `1` dumps as `1`, `1.0` dumps as `1.0`.
104	- `PyBytes{bytes: Uint8Array}`, `PyTuple{items: []}`, `PySet`, `PyDict`,
105	  `PyDate{year,month,day}`, `PyDateTime{...,tzOffsetMinutes}`.
106	- `PyDict`: insertion-ordered, Python key equality (`1`/`1.0`/`true` collide).
107	  `.set(k,v) .get(k) .has(k) .items() .keys() .size .update(other)`.
108	- `PySet`: `.add(v) .has(v) .values() .size`.
109	- `PyDate.isoformat()`, `PyDateTime.isoformat(sep)`.
110	- `pyKey(v)` — canonical hash key; throws `PyTypeError` for unhashable.
111	- `pyTypeName(v)` — `'int'`, `'str'`, `'dict'`, …
112	- `pyReprFloat(n)` — CPython `repr()` of a float (`1.0`, `1e+17`, `1e-05`).
113	- `pyLessThan(a,b)` — Python `<`, throwing `PyTypeError` on mixed types.
114	- `pyEquals(a,b)`.
115	- `pySortInPlace(items, less)` — CPython `list.sort()` comparison order.
116	- `encodeBase64Wrapped(bytes)` — `base64.encodebytes` (76-col wrap, trailing \n).
117	- `decodeBase64(text)` — `binascii.a2b_base64`.
118	
119	### `./tokens.mjs`
120	`StreamStartToken StreamEndToken DirectiveToken DocumentStartToken
121	DocumentEndToken BlockSequenceStartToken BlockMappingStartToken BlockEndToken
122	FlowSequenceStartToken FlowMappingStartToken FlowSequenceEndToken
123	FlowMappingEndToken KeyToken ValueToken BlockEntryToken FlowEntryToken
124	AliasToken AnchorToken TagToken ScalarToken`, plus `isToken(tok, ...classes)`.
125	
126	Positional constructor args mirror PyYAML: value fields first, then
127	`startMark, endMark`. So `new AnchorToken(value, startMark, endMark)`,
128	`new BlockEndToken(startMark, endMark)`,
129	`new ScalarToken(value, plain, startMark, endMark, style)`.
130	Every token has `.id` (`'<scalar>'`, `'['`, `':'`, …) — used verbatim in parser
131	error messages — and `.tokenType`.
132	
133	### `./events.mjs`
134	`StreamStartEvent(startMark, endMark, encoding)`,
135	`StreamEndEvent(startMark, endMark)`,
136	`DocumentStartEvent(startMark, endMark, explicit, version, tags)`,
137	`DocumentEndEvent(startMark, endMark, explicit)`,
138	`AliasEvent(anchor, startMark, endMark)`,
139	`ScalarEvent(anchor, tag, implicit, value, startMark, endMark, style)`,
140	`SequenceStartEvent(anchor, tag, implicit, startMark, endMark, flowStyle)`,
141	`SequenceEndEvent(startMark, endMark)`, `MappingStartEvent(...)` like sequence,
142	`MappingEndEvent(startMark, endMark)`.
143	Also exported for `instanceof` checks: `Event NodeEvent CollectionStartEvent
144	CollectionEndEvent`. Field names are camelCase: `flowStyle`, `startMark`.
145	
146	### `./nodes.mjs`
147	`ScalarNode(tag, value, startMark, endMark, style)`,
148	`SequenceNode(tag, value, startMark, endMark, flowStyle)`,
149	`MappingNode(...)`, base `Node`, `CollectionNode`. Each has `.nodeId`
150	(`'scalar' | 'sequence' | 'mapping'`).
151	
152	## Cross-module method contract (exact names — other agents call these)
153	
154	| Module | Mixin export | Methods other modules call |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| `reader.mjs` | `ReaderMixin` | `peek(i=0)`, `prefix(n=1)`, `forward(n=1)`, `getMark()`; fields `name index line column buffer pointer` |
157	| `scanner.mjs` | `ScannerMixin` | `checkToken(...classes)`, `peekToken()`, `getToken()` |
158	| `parser.mjs` | `ParserMixin` | `checkEvent(...classes)`, `peekEvent()`, `getEvent()` |
159	| `composer.mjs` | `ComposerMixin` | `checkNode()`, `getNode()`, `getSingleNode()` |
160	| `resolver.mjs` | `ResolverMixin` | `resolve(NodeClass, value, implicit)`, `descendResolver(currentNode, currentIndex)`, `ascendResolver()` |
161	| `constructor.mjs` | `ConstructorMixin` | `getSingleData()`, `constructDocument(node)`, `constructObject(node, deep=false)` |
162	| `emitter.mjs` | `EmitterMixin` | `emit(event)`; constructor reads options |
163	| `serializer.mjs` | `SerializerMixin` | `open()`, `serialize(node)`, `close()` |
164	| `representer.mjs` | `RepresenterMixin` | `represent(data)` |
165	
166	`resolve` takes the **node class itself** (`ScalarNode`/`SequenceNode`/
167	`MappingNode`), as PyYAML does, and `implicit` is a 2-element array
168	`[plainImplicit, nonPlainImplicit]`.
169
